questions.stem: Choose the correct form: Neither the teacher nor the students _____ present.
questions.explanation: TYPE 1 — 'neither…nor' rule: verb agrees with the subject CLOSER to it. 'Students' (plural) is closer, so verb is plural → 'are'. Same rule applies to 'either…or'. Trap: many pick 'is' thinking 'neither' forces singular.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: The principal, along with the teachers, _____ arrived.
questions.explanation: TYPE 2 — phrases 'along with / as well as / besides / including' are NON-additive; verb agrees with the FIRST subject only. Principal (singular) → 'has'. The teachers are in a parenthetical, not a co-subject.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: Each of the students _____ a notebook.
questions.explanation: TYPE 6 — 'each / every / either / neither / none / everyone' takes a SINGULAR verb, even when a plural noun follows. 'Each of the students' → 'each' is the subject, 'has' is correct.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: The news _____ surprising.
questions.explanation: TYPE 4 — uncountable-looking-plural nouns (news, mathematics, physics, economics, politics, furniture, information, luggage) take SINGULAR verbs. 'News is'. Trap: the final -s makes it look plural.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: My trousers _____ torn.
questions.explanation: TYPE 5 — 'trousers, scissors, spectacles, pants, goods, thanks, premises, wages, scissors' are ALWAYS plural. 'Trousers are'. These are called pluralia tantum — they have no singular form.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: A number of students _____ absent today.
questions.explanation: TYPE 7 — 'A number of' = many → PLURAL verb. 'The number of' = the count itself → SINGULAR verb. So 'A number of students ARE' but 'The number of students IS'. Classic examiner favourite.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: Ten miles _____ a long distance to walk.
questions.explanation: TYPE 9 — distance, money, time treated as a SINGLE UNIT take a singular verb. 'Ten miles is', 'Five hundred rupees is', 'Two hours is'. The 'ten' makes it look plural, but it functions as one quantity.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: Mathematics _____ my favourite subject.
questions.explanation: TYPE 8 — subject names ending in '-ics' (mathematics, physics, economics, statistics, politics, aerobics) are SINGULAR when referring to the discipline. 'Mathematics is'. They can be plural only in special idiomatic uses ('his politics are…' meaning views).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: There _____ three books on the table.
questions.explanation: TYPE 10 — in 'there is / there are', verb agrees with the REAL subject that FOLLOWS. 'Books' is plural → 'are'. If it were 'There is a book', singular. The 'there' is an empty placeholder, not the subject.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: The jury _____ divided in its opinion.
questions.explanation: TYPE 3 — collective nouns (jury, team, family, committee, government, audience). When acting as a UNIT → singular verb. When MEMBERS act individually → plural. Here 'divided in ITS opinion' — the 'its' signals unit, so 'is'. Compare: 'The jury ARE quarrelling among themselves' (individual action).
questions.subject: English
